subject: Cloud Computing
title: Hypervisors: The Hidden Layer
description: One-minute skill: Hypervisors: The Hidden Layer.

hook.text: Between your operating system and the hardware, there's a hidden layer doing the real work.

buildup.text: A hypervisor creates and manages virtual machines on physical hardware.

discovery.text: Type 1 runs directly on hardware. Type 2 runs on top of an existing operating system.

twist.text: Cloud providers use Type 1 — but they've built custom versions far beyond anything off-the-shelf.

climax.text: AWS built Nitro, its own hypervisor. Google uses custom KVM. Each guards its design as a secret.

punchline.text: The hypervisor is the cloud's invisible foundation.

quiz.question: What does a hypervisor do?
options: Creates and manages virtual machines on physical hardware
Connects data centers to the internet
Encrypts data stored in the cloud

details.summary: A hypervisor is software that creates and manages virtual machines on physical hardware. Type 1 hypervisors run directly on hardware, while Type 2 run on top of an operating system. Cloud providers use Type 1 hypervisors for maximum performance and security.
details.whyItMatters: Hypervisors are the invisible layer that makes cloud computing work. Every virtual machine in the cloud runs on a hypervisor that manages hardware sharing and isolation.
takeaways: Type 1 hypervisors run directly on hardware for best performance
Type 2 hypervisors run on top of an existing operating system
AWS built its own Nitro hypervisor for optimized cloud workloads

faq.question: What hypervisors do cloud providers use?
faq.answer: AWS developed the Nitro hypervisor, a custom lightweight hypervisor. Azure uses a modified version of Hyper-V. Google Cloud uses a custom KVM-based hypervisor. Each provider has optimized their hypervisor for cloud-specific workloads, security, and performance.

faq.question: What is the difference between Type 1 and Type 2?
faq.answer: Type 1 hypervisors like ESXi and Xen run directly on bare metal hardware, offering better performance and security. Type 2 hypervisors like VirtualBox and VMware Workstation run as applications on a host operating system, better suited for development and testing.
